note: Shared oracle for prompt-cache usage normalisation and cache-aware cost. Every SDK must extract the same normalised usage from the same bytes and price it to the same cost (within 1e-12 relative). input_tokens is the whole prompt as the vendor bills it; cache_read/cache_write/cache_write_long_ttl are subsets of it. Bodies are shaped after the vendor docs cited in each note (read 2026-10-21); they are not live captures. expect_cost_usd is computed from conformance/pricing.json by an independent Decimal implementation of: fresh*input + cache_read*cacheRead + (cache_write - long_ttl)*cacheWrite + long_ttl*cacheWriteLongTTL + output*output, tier chosen on the whole prompt.

cases.name: anthropic_json_cache_read_and_5m_write
cases.note: Anthropic input_tokens excludes cache reads and writes (platform.claude.com prompt-caching: total = cache_read + cache_creation + input). Before 0.5.3 the prompt read as 50 tokens and the 102,000 cached tokens priced at $0.

cases.name: anthropic_json_mixed_5m_and_1h_write
cases.note: Numbers from Anthropic's prompt-caching page: cache_creation_input_tokens equals the sum of the cache_creation object; 1h writes bill at 2x input, 5m at 1.25x.

cases.name: anthropic_sse_cache_in_message_start_crosses_long_tier
cases.note: Cache counters arrive in message_start, output in message_delta (MAX merge, rule 12). The whole prompt is 100,050 tokens, over Claude Haiku 5.5's 100,000-token threshold, so the long-prompt rates apply; uncached input alone (50) would have picked the short rates.

cases.name: anthropic_sse_cumulative_message_delta
cases.note: Newer streams repeat input and cache counters, cumulative, in message_delta. MAX-merge must not double them.

cases.name: bedrock_converse_json_cache_details
cases.note: Bedrock Converse TokenUsage: inputTokens excludes cache reads and writes (Bedrock prompt-caching guide: total = inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens); cacheDetails splits writes by ttl.

cases.name: openai_chat_json_cached_tokens
cases.note: OpenAI prompt_tokens is the whole prompt; prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens is the part read from cache, billed at the cached-input price. Before 0.5.3 it billed at the full input price.

cases.name: openai_chat_sse_usage_in_final_chunk
cases.note: Cached tokens arrive only in the final chunk (stream_options.include_usage); intermediates carry usage:null.

cases.name: openai_responses_json_cache_writes_by_ttl
cases.note: GPT-5.6+ Responses usage from OpenAI's prompt-caching guide: ordinary input = 12000 - 4000 - 7000; ttl_30m_tokens bill at the 30m write price, ttl_12h_tokens at the 12h price.

cases.name: openai_responses_sse_response_completed
cases.note: Responses streams carry usage only in response.completed, nested under response.usage.

cases.name: deepseek_json_cache_hit_miss
cases.note: DeepSeek prompt_tokens = prompt_cache_hit_tokens + prompt_cache_miss_tokens (api-docs.deepseek.com); hits bill at the cache-hit price (peak rate stored).

cases.name: gemini_json_cached_content_long_tier
cases.note: Gemini promptTokenCount already includes cachedContentTokenCount (ai.google.dev UsageMetadata). 250,000 is over Gemini 2.5 Pro's 200,000 threshold: long rates, long cache rate.

cases.name: gemini_sse_usage_metadata_every_chunk
cases.note: Gemini streams repeat usageMetadata in each chunk; the last is complete.

cases.name: litellm_proxy_prompt_tokens_already_whole
cases.note: LiteLLM's proxy reports Anthropic usage as prompt_tokens (cache reads and writes already folded in) and repeats cache_read_input_tokens. prompt_tokens present means the prompt is already whole: do not add the cache counters again.

cases.name: hostile_cached_exceeds_prompt
cases.note: A body claiming more cached tokens than prompt tokens is clamped: cache counters are subsets of the prompt, never more.
